question: Rishika travels a certain distance at a speed of 52 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 39 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 56 km/h, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance 1 (d₁) = d

Speed 1 (s₁) = 52 km/hr

Distance 2 (d₂) = 2d

Speed 2 (s₂) = 39 km/hr

Return Distance (d₃) = d + 2d = 3d

Return Speed (s₃) = x km/hr

Average Speed (sₐvg) = 56 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

Total Distance = d₁ + d₂ + d₃

Total Time = d₁/s₁ + d₂/s₂ + d₃/s₃

**Calculations:**

Total Distance = d + 2d + 3d = 6d

Total Time = d/52 + 2d/39 + 3d/x

⇒ 56 = 6d / (d/52 + 2d/39 + 3d/x)

⇒ 56 = 6 / (1/52 + 2/39 + 3/x)

⇒ 1/52 + 2/39 + 3/x = 6/56

⇒ 1/52 + 2/39 + 3/x = 3/28

⇒ (3 + 8)/156 + 3/x = 3/28

⇒ 11/156 + 3/x = 3/28

⇒ 3/x = 3/28 - 11/156

⇒ 3/x = (3 × 39 - 11 × 7) / 1092

⇒ 3/x = (117 - 77) / 1092

⇒ 3/x = 40 / 1092

⇒ x = (3 × 1092) / 40

⇒ x = 3276 / 40

⇒ x = 81.9

**∴ The speed for the return journey is 81.9 km/hr.**
